dynamic-symmetry.translation: Active Proportional Symmetry Commensurable in Square
dynamic-symmetry.definition: Proportional architecture derived from organic growth (phyllotaxis and equiangular shells) and Euclidean commensurability in square, built upon root-rectangles (√2, √3, √5) and the whirling-square golden rectangle (φ ≈ 1.6180...) whose diagonals and reciprocals subdivide areas into self-similar gnomonic parts.

static-symmetry.translation: Passive Symmetry Based on Fixed Units and Regular Polygons
static-symmetry.definition: Symmetry based on linear commensurability, regular polygons (square, equilateral triangle, hexagon, octagon), and static modular repetition—characteristic of Roman, Byzantine, Gothic, and Renaissance decorative art, contrasted by Hambidge with the active dynamic proportion of classical Greek design and living growth.

commensurable-in-square.translation: Commensurable in Square / Commensurable in Power
commensurable-in-square.definition: Magnitudes whose linear lengths are irrational with respect to one another (such as 1 and √2, √3, √5) yet whose squares (quadrances) have exact integer ratios (1 : 2 : 3 : 4 : 5). Identified by Jay Hambidge (1919–1920) as the exact classical origin of 'Dynamic Symmetry'.

root-rectangle.definition: A rectangle whose side length is the square root of an integer (√2, √3, √4 = 2, √5) constructed on a unit end. Successive root rectangles unfold by swinging the diagonal of each preceding rectangle down to the extended baseline, incrementing the side quadrance by exact integer steps Q = 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5.

reciprocal-rectangle.definition: A geometrically similar rectangle custom-scaled so that the end of the parent rectangle becomes the side of the reciprocal, having width 1/r for a parent of ratio r. The diagonal of the reciprocal intersects the diagonal of the parent at exact perpendicular spread s = 1 (90°).

whirling-square-rectangle.definition: The rectangle of aspect ratio 1 : φ (φ = (1 + √5)/2 ≈ 1.618034). Detaching an exact square leaves a reciprocal golden rectangle of width 1/φ = φ - 1 ≈ 0.618034; repeated gnomonic square detachment forms a spiral of squares 'whirling' toward the intersection of perpendicular diagonals.

gnomon.definition: Originally the carpenter's L-square surrounding a square to make a larger square (Aristotle, Categories 15a30; Euclid II Def. 2), generalized by Hero of Alexandria (Def. 58) to any figure whose addition to a given figure leaves the composite figure geometrically similar to the original.

equiangular-spiral.definition: The planar growth curve studied by Descartes, Bernoulli, and Thompson whose tangent at every point makes a constant angle α with the radius vector OP, so that continuous terminal accretion increases size without altering geometric form.

phyllotaxis.definition: The mathematical arrangement of leaves, scales, and florets around a stem or capitulum (e.g. sunflower seed heads), governed by the golden angle divergence (137° 30′ 28″) and visible intersecting parastichy spiral pairs (34/55, 55/89, 89/144).

parastichy.definition: One of the prominent visible intersecting contact spirals on a cylindrical plant stem or discoidal flower head, arranged in antagonistic left- and right-winding families whose curve counts form consecutive Fibonacci numbers.

divergence-angle.definition: The azimuthal angular step around the stem axis between consecutively initiated primordia (n and n+1) along the genetic spiral, converging to 360° × (1 - 1/φ) ≈ 137.5077°.

quadrance.translation: Squared Distance Q(A, B) = (x₂ - x₁)² + (y₂ - y₁)²
quadrance.definition: The fundamental measure of separation in Rational Trigonometry, replacing square-root distances with exact rational values. Root rectangles have consecutive integer quadrances Q = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

spread.translation: Squared Sine s(l₁, l₂) = sin² θ
spread.definition: The fundamental measure of line opening in Rational Trigonometry, replacing angles with exact rational values. Perpendicular lines (such as a rectangle's diagonal and its reciprocal diagonal) have exact spread s = 1.
